summary: Bonner County, Idaho cabin and barn reported in 1925, used by fire wardens by 1927, later listed abandoned and gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as abandoned and gone; no source describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Cabin and barn per the two history pages; a May 1925 newspaper item reports a new lookout being built
Fire wardens report says one lookout covered the Careywood, Granite and Cocolalla district

evidence.supports: cabin and barn in 1925; listed abandoned

evidence.quote: a documented staffing history for this lookout

evidence.supports: May 1925 newspaper: new lookout being built about three miles NW of Careywood
evidence.quote: J.R. Winnington reports the building of a new lookout on Huckleberry mountain, three miles northwest of Careywood.

evidence.supports: January 1927 fire wardens report: one lookout covered the Careywood, Granite and Cocolalla district
evidence.quote: Careywood, Granite and Cocolalla district--One lookout on Huckleberry Mountain sec. 35, township 55, range 3W., was able to cover this district.

evidence.supports: telephone line from the lookout to the Interstate Utilities main line
evidence.quote: Four miles of metallic telephone line was strung from Huckleberry lookout

evidence.supports: index lists the Bonner site as Ground, Gone

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two history pages, a 1925 newspaper item and a 1927 fire wardens report, both as quoted on the weebly page (the newspaper and report themselves were not read). Nothing describes the site today and no source gives an access level, so facts.access is omitted. The weebly entry shows a 'Removed' label with no date; not used. Location: the brief's three coordinate sets differ by roughly 2 km (FFLA 48.07312/-116.67517 as in the brief; Idaho 48.06249/-116.6959; West US 48.0842/-116.6863); not checked on a map. Do not confuse with two other Huckleberry Mountain lookouts: the Idaho Fire Lookouts 'Huckleberry Mountain Lookout' page without the -2 suffix (Coeur d'Alene NF, 4,865 ft, tower removed 1950) and a Pend Oreille County, Washington Huckleberry Mountain that appeared in search with its own 1925 records. Neither was used.
